_comment: T021 demo fixture seed, loaded by `agile run --seed` (packages/cli/src/commands/run.ts) via the daemon's validating StateStore — never written as raw .agile/ files. product.md is the one exception (init.ts's own stub is a plain file, not a StateStore entity).
productMd:
# Product

demo-project is a tiny in-memory task tracker (fixtures/demo-project/src/tasks.ts) — the T021 end-to-end demo's target, not a real product. Non-goals: persistence, auth, a UI. Glossary: a *task* has a title, an ISO `dueDate`, and a `done` flag.

entry.title: Code quality baseline
entry.rationale: Seeded baseline spec for the demo epic — every ticket's implementation is checked against it.

oracle.body:
# SPEC-quality-001: Code quality baseline

1. Every public function validates its inputs and throws a descriptive `Error` on invalid input — never returns a silently wrong result.
2. No debug `console.log`/`console.debug` calls ship in `src/`.

entry.title: Task listing order
entry.rationale: Seeded spec for the demo epic's second ticket — contains the planted self-contradiction T021 requires.

oracle.body:
# SPEC-tasks-002: Task listing order

1. `listTasks()` returns tasks sorted ascending by `dueDate`.
2. `listTasks()` must preserve insertion order and never reorder tasks.

(Clauses 1 and 2 contradict each other for any two tasks created out of due-date order — this is the seeded contradiction ticket TKT-1002's engineer is expected to discover, not silently pick one reading of.)

acceptance: TaskStore.completeTask(id) sets that task's done to true and returns the updated task
completeTask throws a descriptive Error for an unknown id (SPEC-quality-001 clause 1)
listTasks() returns tasks sorted ascending by dueDate (SPEC-tasks-002 clause 1)
overdueTasks(now) returns every task whose dueDate is before now, in listTasks()'s order

discovery._comment: Scripted for TKT-1002's engineer in offline/--fake mode (no live model to notice the contradiction on its own) — see run.ts's driveEngineerWork.
discovery.proposed: SPEC-tasks-002 clauses 1 and 2 contradict each other; resolve by keeping clause 1 (sort ascending by due date) and retiring clause 2.

entry.title: listTasks() sorts ascending by due date; clause 2 (insertion order) is retired
entry.rationale: SPEC-tasks-002 clauses 1 and 2 contradicted each other; clause 1 (sort ascending by due date) is kept, clause 2 (insertion order) is retired.

decision.body:
# DEC-0001

SPEC-tasks-002 clause 1 (sort ascending by `dueDate`) wins; clause 2 (preserve insertion order) is retired as contradictory. `listTasks()` and anything built on it (TKT-1003's `overdueTasks`) must sort ascending by `dueDate`.
